## What the company does

Dell Technologies Inc. is based in Round Rock, Texas. It reports two segments. The Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) sells servers, storage and networking. The Client Solutions Group (CSG) sells personal computers and peripherals. Dell Financial Services supplies customer financing and is a real internal cash-flow engine, not a footnote.

In the quarter ended 31 July 2026 (Dell fiscal 2027 second quarter), total revenue was $46.971 billion, up 58% from a year earlier. ISG was $31.782 billion, about 68% of revenue. CSG was $15.034 billion, about 32%. AI-optimised servers alone were $16.401 billion, about 35% of all revenue ([Dell Q2 FY27 release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2026~09~dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results.htm)). Full-year fiscal 2026, ended 30 January 2026, had revenue of $113.538 billion.

## The demand record

Dell reports a long sequence of AI order figures. These run from $17.7 billion in the first half of fiscal 2026, to $12.3 billion in fiscal 2026 third quarter, to more than $64 billion for full-year fiscal 2026, to $24.4 billion in fiscal 2027 first quarter, to $60.9 billion in fiscal 2027 second quarter. The reported AI backlog was $18.4 billion at the end of fiscal 2026 third quarter, $43 billion at the end of fiscal 2026, and a record $95 billion at the end of fiscal 2027 second quarter. The AI customer base grew from 5,000 to 6,500 in one quarter ([TIKR summary](https://www.tikr.com/blog/dell-booked-60-9-billion-in-ai-orders-this-quarter)).

Dell raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance three times: to $138-142 billion revenue on 26 February 2026, to about $167 billion on 28 May 2026, and to about $192 billion revenue with about $74 billion of AI server revenue on 1 September 2026.

## The open question

The ISG operating margin was 15.0% of ISG revenue in fiscal 2027 second quarter, up 620 basis points from a year earlier. That figure covers servers, storage and networking together. Dell does not disclose a margin for the AI server line. Barclays estimates that line at about 5%, and this is an analyst estimate, not a company figure. Both facts can be true at once: a strong segment margin, with a much thinner AI server margin inside it.

Memory is the binding input cost. Dell says it reprices almost daily and locks its largest customers into three- to five-year deals, per comments by Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke ([Supply Chain Dive](https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/dell-hpe-server-supply-upended-by-memory-crunch/822273)). Higher memory prices lift Dell's revenue and its costs at the same time.

Cash needs watching. In fiscal 2027 second quarter, cash from operations fell 13% to $2.225 billion while revenue rose 58%. Dell separately reported adjusted free cash flow of $8.149 billion. Dell Financial Services financing receivables look like the main item in that gap, but Dell has not published the bridge ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/dell-stocks-fall-9-4-181327597.html)). At 31 January 2026, liabilities of $103.756 billion exceeded assets of $101.286 billion, so book equity was negative.

## Connected event

On 14 October 2026, Barclays cut Dell to Equal Weight and lowered its price target to $574 from $603. Dell fell 11.4% that day and about 6.6% more on 15 October. See the linked market event page.

## What would settle the debate

- Dell's own gross or operating margin for AI-optimised servers.
- Unit shipments or average selling prices, which would separate volume growth from cost pass-through.
- A bridge from the company-defined $95 billion AI backlog to the standard remaining performance obligation of about $82 billion at 30 January 2026.
- A reconciliation of GAAP cash from operations to adjusted free cash flow.

A partnership payment changes cash and risk; it does not change commercial performance. ## The price move As of 15 October 2026 20:50 UTC, NVAX was up 14.3% over one week, 28.3% over one month and 62.6% over three months, and 1.3% on the day. Over five years it is down 92.3% (Market Explorer observation). A Zopedia snapshot at 9 October 2026 04:00 UTC put the close at $12.745. The 5-day return was +21.7%, the 21-day +36.9%, the 63-day +43.0%. The 14-day RSI was 68.1, near the 70 level that often marks an overbought market. The 20-day annualised volatility was 95%. Price sat about 90% up its recent channel, with resistance at $13.385 and support at $7.15 ([NVAX — Novavax](https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/NVAX/)). In the week of 5–7 October 2026, NVAX rose about 20%. Reports show a close of $12.56 on 5 October, up 20.08% on about 28.5 million shares; an intraday print of $12.12, up 15.9%, as a new 52-week high; and a print of $12.62, up 20.65%, about $2.16 above a prior close of $10.46. All three imply a prior close near $10.46, so they probably describe the same session at different times. One source shows an $11.01 close for 8 October, which does not agree with the $12.745 snapshot. The daily close series for 1–9 October 2026 is not settled ([Novavax (NVAX) Surge, Early October 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-novavax-stock-surging-today-93CH-4932717)). ## Reported drivers Three causes are reported, not confirmed: - **An FDA-related catalyst.** An opened FDA page lists Nuvaxovid as approved, but the page is archived with an 08 July 2026 expiry. It does not confirm a new October 2026 action. - **A Sanofi agreement**, reported as a $500 million upfront payment, up to $700 million in future milestones, and royalties on future sales. This is the single most important number in the file. The exact terms, the 2026 triggers and the timing are not confirmed. - **Vaccine-sector strength.** Benzinga reported on 9–10 October 2026 that a new NIH-backed initiative to speed up personalised cancer vaccine development sent MRNA, BNTX and NVAX higher; live evidence says the NIH plans a public-private cancer vaccine programme starting in December, focused on pancreatic and liver cancer ([A New War on Cancer?](https://benzinga.com/news/health-care/26/10/62283036/a-new-war-on-cancer-nihs-vaccine-initiative-sparks-biotech-stock-rally), [Vaccine Stocks Rally](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/vaccine-stocks-rally-reports-u-141200740.html)). On the same day, 24/7 Wall St reported NVAX at $12.77, up 16% (its own quick-read block said 14%), MRNA at $219.30, up 11%, MRK at $146.18, up 3%, the iShares Biotechnology ETF up 3% and SPY up 0.5% ([24/7 Wall St via AOL](https://benzinga.com/news/health-care/26/10/62283036/a-new-war-on-cancer-nihs-vaccine-initiative-sparks-biotech-stock-rally)). ## What the company's own numbers show Period 2026Q1 (report date 31 March 2026): - Revenue $139.5 million, down 79.1% from a year earlier. The year-earlier quarter was far larger, and this revenue line is lumpy because it depends on partner payments and seasonal vaccine sales. - Net income -$9.5 million, against -$202.4 million in 2025Q3. - Operating cash flow -$32.4 million. - Free cash flow +$6.1 million, the first positive reading since 2025Q3. - Stockholders' equity -$144.8 million. - Total assets $1,043.2 million; total liabilities $1,187.9 million. Negative stockholders' equity has been the normal state since late 2021, with only brief positive readings. Liabilities have exceeded assets over the same period. Negative equity is a chronic condition, not a new one. ## Bull hypothesis **Mechanism.** Novavax has shifted from paying for its own manufacturing and sales to collecting partner payments. If the Sanofi agreement delivers a $500 million upfront, up to $700 million in milestones and a royalty stream, that cash arrives without a matching cost, which extends runway and makes revenue less dependent on the company's own commercial spending. At the same time, the net loss has narrowed sharply and free cash flow turned positive in 2026Q1.
